extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and readers interested in scholarly publishing and peer review (especially in mathematics)
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and expectations for peer review and editorial decision-making in mathematics journals, including number of reviewers, screening practices, and governance (e.g., EIC changes and editorial-board consultation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness of mathematical refereeing (line-by-line correctness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in mathematics requires not only an assessment of impact and significance but also a 'line-by-line painstaking check for correctness of the results.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should verify completeness and correctness; this is time-consuming and makes referees a scarce and valuable resource. Expect detailed, technical checking rather than cursory commentary. Anti-pattern: treating mathematical papers like other disciplines where superficial checks of impact suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of independent peer reviewers per paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor & Francis: 'Ensuring that every published article has been fully reviewed by at least two peers is standard practice for all Taylor & Francis Mathematics and Statistics journals and common across academic publishing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher policy may require two full peer reviews per article. The editorial community debate: imposing multiple full reviews can strain reviewer supply or dilute review quality if not implemented with regard for field-specific needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of doubling expected reviews (reviewer pool and quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors warned that 'Doubling the number of expected reviews will quickly either deplete the pool of willing reviewers or vastly dilute the quality of their reviews, and both of these are unacceptable outcomes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When changing review expectations, consider reviewer availability and quality trade-offs. Scoring guidance: policies that increase reviewer counts should include mechanisms to ensure review quality and sustainable reviewer recruitment; otherwise they may be counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quick opinions as a screening measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals (and the editors) use or propose a 'quick opinion' substitute for one full review to decide whether a paper merits an in-depth review; 'several leading mathematics journals will request "quick opinions" of experts to decide whether the paper should get an in-depth review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick opinions serve as lightweight expert triage to filter submissions before commissioning full, time-consuming reviews. Guidance: implement quick opinions transparently and distinguish them from full referee reports to preserve standards without overburdening reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor appraisal before external peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are first appraised by the editor and then, 'if found suitable for further consideration,' are peer-reviewed by independent referees (journal website description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial triage is an expected workflow step; editors should apply expertise to screen for suitability before sending papers to referees. This preserves reviewer effort for papers that merit full review. Guidance includes clear criteria for 'suitable for further consideration.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-board consultation for major policy or personnel changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors criticized the publisher for ousting the editor-in-chief in a 'cloak-and-dagger removal' and implementing policy changes 'without consulting with the board.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice (implied): consult the editorial board about substantive changes to review policies or leadership; lack of consultation is described as unacceptable and a governance failing. Example anti-pattern: unilateral major decisions by publisher without board input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-board size vs. referee sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors argued that 'drastically increase[ing] the size of the editorial board' does not address reviewer shortage because referees are experts outside the editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy changes that expand the board should not be presented as a fix for reviewer scarcity; instead, journals should recognize that independent referees are typically external experts and plan reviewer recruitment and incentives accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics community approach to reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The math field 'actively deals with the reproducibility crisis in other subjects by ensuring papers are complete and correct. This is time consuming,' (Alan Logan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility in mathematics is enforced by requiring complete proofs and correctness checks. Evaluative guidance: accept only submissions that enable line-by-line verification; recognize the time cost when designing review expectations and timelines.
